newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Oxy lifts Cano Limon Force Majeure.
newsitem.headline: Oxy lifts Cano Limon Force Majeure.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said that it had lifted force majeure on the Cano Limon oil field in northeast Colombia after production resumed at the field Friday afternoon.
A company spokesman confirmed that it had lifted the measure shortly after he said the state oil company Ecopetrol announced that it had lifted its Force Majeure on Cano Limon loadings.
"We've done the same in the field (lift force majeure) and production has resumed," the spokesman said.

Occidental declared force majeure on the 175,000 barrel per day field on July 10 after dynamite attacks by leftist rebels crippled the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline and forced the company to shut in its Cano Limon production.

Ecopetrol had declared force majeure on loadings on July 6 and repair work on the pipeline was delayed earlier this week by a continuing rebel presence near the sites where the back-to-back dynamite attacks occurred.

Friday's reopening of the pipeline -- and the return to production at Cano Limon -- closes one of the grimest chapters in the history of the pipeline, which opened in 1986 and has been dynamited more than 470 times since then.

Ten soliders were killed by guerrillas when they attempted to secure an area in northeast Arauca province where one of the pipeline blasts occurred on July 10. Twenty other soliders and one civilian crew member died earlier this month when rebels shot down a helicopter ferrying them to a public security zone, or "hot spot," adjacent to the pipeline.
